main_body: Log cabin with a large snow-covered roof slope (rows 7-50) over a vertical plank front wall with a double arched door and two lit windows (rows 52-76)
top_band: Snow roof slope, near-white to pale blue (L 249/228/200) from rows 8 to about 50, ending in a lighter eave lip with icicles. Below it the dark brown plank wall begins at row 52.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly separate top surface, as in the Beodeul house references where the tile roof reads as the top slope above the wall. A bright snow eave band at rows 48-50 marks the front edge. Directly under it, icicles and a dark row at about row 51 act as the eave shadow. The wall below is a distinct, much darker vertical face with its own plank shading. The windows have snow sills, and the door has iron straps and a dark centre seam, so they read as inset. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 lightness steps (249, 228, 200, 166, 130) in scalloped clumps. The wood has several browns with vertical grain, and the roof has dark moss patches and icicles. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark navy beside snow, dark brown beside wood). Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Median colours per tile is 9, against 11 for the stone reference and 18 for the other. The 42 total colours are fewer than the 66 and 185 in the references, so density is somewhat lower but still close to the stone reference. The repeating snow scallops are a little uniform, but the piece would sit acceptably beside the references.
